as_told.title: Westall school mass sighting and landing

plain: In 1966, at Westall in Australia, a crowd of schoolchildren and a teacher are said to have watched a disc-shaped craft in the sky, and some say it landed. James Fox, a documentary filmmaker who investigates UFO cases, went to look into what he calls this "landing case." He says the witnesses he met told him "we've been going at it for 50 years." He later puts the crowd at "300 plus witnesses" watching "this disc zip around in the sky," and credits two others, Shane Ryan and James Rigney. A commentator named Marik von Rennenkampff gives his own summary without naming a source. He says 200 or 300 students and a teacher saw "a silver disc sort of banked on its side" that then took off at 1,000 miles an hour, and he says nothing of a landing. A retired Army officer named Karl Nell brings up Westall secondhand, as an "almost similar identical incident" to another sighting at a school. The case is told because so many ordinary witnesses saw the same thing at once.
